stem.bridgelab.challenge_footbridge_stor: A 20 m footbridge over a stream. Keep walkers safe and spend as little as possible.
stem.bridgelab.challenge_county_road_sto: A 40 m crossing for farm traffic, modelled as a heavy load at every joint. Make it safe for the lowest cost.
stem.bridgelab.challenge_featherweight_s: A 30 m bridge that will be flown in by helicopter. It needs extra safety margin, and every kilogram counts.
stem.bridgelab.challenge_long_span_story: A 70 m gap with no pier allowed in the river. Make it safe for the lowest cost.
stem.bridgelab.challenge_site: Span {span} m · {bays} bays · {load} kN at each joint · uniform load
stem.bridgelab.challenge_goal_mass: Safety factor {sf} or more, as light as possible
stem.bridgelab.challenge_goal_cost: Safety factor {sf} or more, as cheap as possible
stem.bridgelab.challenge_intro: Each challenge fixes the site and the load. You choose the truss style, height, material, cross-section and bracing. One star for a safe bridge; more stars for using less money or material.
stem.bridgelab.challenge_not_passing: Not recorded yet: every requirement must be met first.
stem.bridgelab.challenge_no_better: Your saved design is already as good or better. Try for a lower score.
stem.bridgelab.challenge_hint_1: Check the design brief: is the bridge limited by yield (the material crushing or tearing) or by buckling (a slender member bowing sideways)?
stem.bridgelab.challenge_hint_2: A deeper truss lowers the chord forces, and closer lateral bracing shortens the length a top chord can buckle over.
stem.bridgelab.challenge_hint_3: Compare materials by strength per dollar or per kilogram, not by strength alone. The cost optimizer further down can size a section for your geometry.
stem.bridgelab.challenge_check_material: Material: wood, steel or FRP composite
stem.bridgelab.challenge_material_why: Stone, cast iron and reinforced concrete are left out because this simple axial model cannot represent how they carry tension.
